four_layer_diagnosis.claim_alignment: unclear (SD-082) -- for the first time in this lineage the readiness conjunction held, the control the 822e autopsy demanded was present, and the criterion was reachable (the in-loop positive control reaches an index of 5.28; the index ceiling is K = 32), so the run DID let registry leg H1 -- 'the TRAINED rule->bias readout adds candidate-discrimination beyond its initialisation' -- express itself. H1 is NULL at adequate power for rejection: the observed mean D 0.063 sits 4.9 standard errors below the pre-registered 0.5 (t(4) = -4.88, p < 0.005 one-sided). That null is on H1, a proposition the claim text does not assert: SD-082's three registered predicates -- common-mode-invariant (centering engaged), gradient-trainable (every tensor moved; 69-70 updates), maps rule_state to a per-candidate bias (argmax flips on 15% of ticks) -- were each POSITIVELY observed. It is NOT stamped weakens because (a) the pre-registered rule reserves weakens for D <= -0.5 (training REMOVES discrimination), which is not the negation of H1; (b) that branch was UNREACHABLE on this run by construction -- the weakens_route_controls (dead-ReLU masks comparable on every ON cell, AND trained head failing absolute C1) both read false, because 4/5 ON cells exceed the 0.50 dead-ReLU floor and C1 passed -- so the rule was two-valued (supports / inconclusive) whatever D was (red-team F3); and (c) the learning signal's CONTENT is unmeasured (only the update count is recorded). unclear (SD-078) -- co-tag; C4 emits inconclusive by its own detectability clause (|t| 0.17 < 2.13).

four_layer_diagnosis.prerequisites: present -- SD-078 rule pool differentiates on ARM_ON in 5/5 seeds (rule_state_diff 0.62-0.77; OFF pinned at 0.0), z_world cone 0.933 >= 0.9, SD-082's per-candidate-summary amend engaged (summary spread survives centering, 0 fallbacks, 0 degenerate ticks), raw-stage replica matches substrate to 7.5e-9.
four_layer_diagnosis.implementation: partial -- the readout IS wired, gradient-trainable and candidate-discriminating; but its scale-free discrimination INDEX after training is statistically indistinguishable from the init head's on ARM_ON (D ~ 0), while the init head already clears the absolute C1 floor on the same 4/5 seeds. The trained head is nevertheless NOT the init head: it is a measurably different function -- training reduced argmax flips relative to the init head in 10 of 10 cells (pooled 260 vs 493; sign test p = 0.001; ON 148 vs 194, OFF 112 vs 299), and on the pinned-pool ARM_OFF the index moved by up to -2.95 (seed 633 init 4.70 -> trained 1.69); last-layer weights moved 16-32% of their init norm (red-team F2). So the readout was shaped by training, in a direction that halves the rate at which rule_state changes the cross-candidate argmax without changing the index. Hidden ReLU dead fraction 0.44-0.66 on ARM_ON (H4) -- the same fractions that foreclosed the weakens branch.
four_layer_diagnosis.measurement: partial -- the instrument's inputs are sound (in-run init distribution measured, paired per tick, real Frobenius liveness distance scoped to ARM_ON, all five 822e requirements implemented). Two defects in what it can EMIT: (i) the weakens branch was unreachable on this run by construction (weakens_route_controls both false: dead_relu_masks_comparable_all_on_cells false with 4/5 ON cells >= 0.50 dead; trained_head_fails_absolute_c1 false), so one of the claim's three pre-registered outcomes was foreclosed before D was read; (ii) the rule has no branch for the outcome it found -- H1 rejected at adequate power (D ~ 0, CI excluding +0.5) -- and labels it inconclusive. Also: the supports rule (mean D >= 0.5 AND D>0 on 4/5) has only ~50% power at a true D of 0.5 (99% at 0.7), so 'a consistent 0.5 would have registered' is not a claim this design supports (red-team F5); what IS well-powered is rejecting D >= 0.5 on the observed sd. Recording gaps for the next run: per-update gradient norm, per-episode return variance, per-episode flip-rate trajectory, step-direction persistence (||sum of steps|| / sum of ||steps||).
four_layer_diagnosis.integration: coupled -- E2 rollout -> candidate summaries -> centered rule readout -> raw bias -> tanh -> E3 argmax; flips occur (rule_flip_observed true).
four_layer_diagnosis.scale: adequate for REJECTING H1 at 0.5 (t(4) = -4.9 on the observed sd); the supports rule itself is under-powered at exactly 0.5 (50%) and adequate at 0.7 (99%); C4 by design inconclusive at n=5 (contrast_sd 0.90; ~59 seeds for the 0.25 margin).

biological_reference.closest_mechanism: corticostriatal rule-to-action readout (lateral PFC rule state biasing striatal action selection)
dependencies: a readout shaped by dense, temporally local credit (here: an episode-summed harm return assigned to every selection in the episode, one Adam step per P1 episode, 69-70 steps)
a candidate set with summary-level structure to read (present; the init head already reads it)
biological_reference.divergence: The learning rule, not the readout topology. Under REINFORCE with an episode-summed return the per-step gradient direction is weakly persistent: the last layer's measured Frobenius movement (0.023-0.045 over 69-70 steps) matches a direction-inconsistent walk at lr 5e-4 (random-sign ~0.025; SNR ~1 ~0.041) and uses 12-23% of the consistent-sign budget (0.198); a zero gradient would move Adam not at all. Biological readouts of this kind are shaped by dense credit with a persistent direction. Load-bearing for the next probe (learning-signal axis), not for the claim's truth.

targets.recommended_evidence_quality_note: [2026-09-09 failure_autopsy_V3-EXQ-822f_2026-09-09, Fable cross-model red-team CONTESTED on assertions, five findings folded in] V3-EXQ-822f (evidence, design-changed successor to 822e per its confirmed autopsy: init-head control, trained-minus-init index load-bearing, new seeds 611-655, ARM_ON-scoped Frobenius liveness gate, C4 detectability-scoped; FAIL, ree-worker-3, 2h58m) ran with readiness 19/19 met for the first time in the lineage. SD-082: inconclusive per the pre-registered rule. Content: registry leg H1 -- 'the TRAINED readout adds candidate-discrimination beyond its initialisation' -- is REJECTED at adequate power: paired trained-minus-init index on ARM_ON D = +0.32/-0.09/-0.00/+0.22/-0.14, mean 0.063 (sd 0.20, se 0.09; t(4) = -4.9 against the pre-registered 0.5; the criterion was reachable: positive control 5.28, index ceiling 32); the init head clears the absolute C1 floor on the same 4/5 seeds as the trained head. This is a null on H1, NOT on SD-082's own text: its three predicates (common-mode-invariant; gradient-trainable; maps rule_state to a per-candidate bias) were each positively observed (centering engaged; every tensor moved over 69-70 updates; argmax flips on 15% of ticks). Nor is it 'training did nothing': the trained head flips the argmax LESS than the init head in 10/10 cells (260 vs 493 pooled, p = 0.001) and moved the pinned-pool OFF-arm index by up to -2.95 -- training shaped the readout toward a LESS rule-sensitive function at unchanged index. Not weakens because (i) the mirrored clause tests 'training removes discrimination', not H1's negation, and (ii) that branch was unreachable on this run by construction: the weakens_route_controls both read false (4/5 ON cells above the 0.50 dead-ReLU floor; absolute C1 passed), so the rule was two-valued here. Learning signal: an episode-summed harm return assigned to every P1 selection; the last layer's 0.023-0.045 Frobenius movement matches a direction-inconsistent gradient walk (random-sign ~0.025 at lr 5e-4 over 70 steps; zero gradient would move Adam 0), and return variance is unrecorded (n_p1_updates 69-70 is not evidence the return varied: the EMA baseline starts at 0 so stale buffer entries carry advantage under a constant return). SD-078: co-tag; C4 inconclusive by its own detectability clause (2/5 seeds clear 0.25, mean 0.069, sd 0.90, t-like 0.17 < 2.13; ~59 seeds for the margin). Neither claim moves. REFUSED: 822g or any same-design letter -- the missing axis is signal content and sign, not P1 length (a direction-inconsistent walk grows as sqrt(steps)). OWED: a learning-signal diagnostic under a NEW EXQ (per-update gradient norm and direction persistence, per-episode return variance and flip-rate trajectory, sign of the advantage on flip vs non-flip selections, a dense-credit positive control), and the registry's unassigned legs H2/H3/H4 each need their own probe -- H4 (dead ReLU) now with raised priority, since the same fractions foreclosed the weakens branch.

suggested_probes.sketch: Diagnostic, no arm contrast needed, 3-5 seeds: record per-P1-update gradient norm on rule_bias_head, per-tensor step direction persistence (||sum of steps|| / sum of ||steps||), per-episode return variance, per-episode trained-head flip rate (trajectory), and the sign of the advantage on flip vs non-flip selections; positive control = the same head trained on a dense synthetic credit (a known candidate-discriminating function of rule_state) must move D past 0.5 with persistence near 1. Nulls: (noisy) persistence and return variance are non-trivial; (sign) the advantage on flip selections is not negative and the flip-rate trajectory is flat.

Re-initialise the head with a smaller dead fraction (LeakyReLU or init scale) and re-measure the init-head index spread, D, and whether the weakens_route_controls become live; null: D and the dead-mask comparability are unchanged when dead fraction drops below 0.25.

Hidden-mask decomposition of the raw index: hold the head fixed, permute candidate summaries across candidates; null: the index collapses to the iid reference when summaries are shuffled (summary geometry, not rule information, carries it).

fanout_recommendation.note: GOV-FANOUT-1: the bottleneck is a discrimination (init index vs noisy signal vs signal sign vs capacity vs upstream geometry), not a build. The learning-signal probe adjudicates two legs under one measurement and should go first; do not re-pose C1' with more seeds.

learning_extracted: The lineage's discrimination INDEX is init-like: the deep-copied init head clears the absolute C1 floor on the same 4/5 ON seeds as the trained head (same failing seed, 622); on a pinned single-rule pool (OFF/seed633, rule_state_diff 0.0) the init index is 4.70 against an iid reference of 5.15 -- the raw index reads summary geometry through a random projection, not rule information. But the trained head is NOT the init head: training reduced argmax flips in 10 of 10 cells (260 vs 493 pooled; p = 0.001) and moved the OFF-arm index by up to -2.95; last-layer weights moved 16-32% of their init norm. 'Within the init spread' describes the index, not the function.

The head moved as an optimiser with a direction-INCONSISTENT gradient would: last-layer Frobenius movement 0.023-0.045 over 69-70 Adam steps at lr 5e-4 matches a random-sign walk (~0.025) to SNR~1 (~0.041) and uses 12-23% of the consistent-sign budget (0.198); a zero gradient would not move Adam at all. The update count (69-70) is not evidence the return varied -- the EMA baseline starts at 0, so stale buffer entries carry advantage under a constant return. Gradient content and direction persistence are unrecorded.

The three-valued rule was two-valued on this run: the weakens branch requires dead-ReLU masks comparable on every ON cell (4/5 cells were above the 0.50 floor) AND the trained head failing absolute C1 (it passed), so weakens could not have fired for any D. A pre-registered branch that a control can foreclose must report the foreclosure as an outcome, and a one-sided requirement needs a branch for 'no trained increment at adequate power' (D ~ 0, CI excluding +0.5), which is what was found.

The supports rule (mean D >= 0.5 AND D>0 on 4/5) has ~50% power at a true D of 0.5 and ~99% at 0.7; what the design does well is REJECT D >= 0.5 on the observed sd (t(4) = -4.9). State power claims against the rule that fires, not against the t critical value.
